title: Challenge: Create a BMI Calculator
summary: Introduces the interactive BMI calculator challenge: write a bmiCalculator function that takes weight then height and returns the BMI, then use the Check Solution button. The walkthrough comes in the next lecture.

concepts.heading: Challenge requirements
points: BMI formula: weight divided by height squared, with weight in kilograms and height in metres.
The function must be named bmiCalculator and return the BMI so that a line such as var bmi = bmiCalculator(weight, height); stores the result.
Parameter order matters: weight first, then height, to match the provided calling line.
Workflow: copy the starter code from index.js into a DevTools Snippet (or any JS runner), write the function, console.log the bmi variable and compare with an online BMI calculator.
When satisfied, press Check Solution in the exercise page; the solution video follows in the next lecture.

task.name: BMI calculator function
task.starting_point: Starter index.js with the calling line var bmi = bmiCalculator(weight, height); in the exercise page.
task.goal: Create bmiCalculator(weight, height) returning the BMI.
steps: Declare function bmiCalculator with parameters weight then height.
Compute weight / height squared (Math.pow(height, 2) or height * height).
Return the value (the reference solution rounds with Math.round).
Log the result and compare with an online BMI calculator.
task.expected_result: For example 65 kg and 1.8 m gives about 20 when rounded.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 14 - Introduction to Javascript ES6/14.15 - Challenge - Create a BMI Calculator

pitfalls: (Extra) Writing weight / height * height cancels out; the squared height needs grouping or Math.pow.
Passing arguments in the wrong order.
(Extra) The exercise says nothing about rounding in this video; the reference repo rounds to a whole number.

playground.coverage: Fully covers the task: bmiCalculator(weight, height), brackets warning, Math.round, test value of 65 kg and 1.8 m, and a pointer to section 15.
gaps_and_ideas: Add the parameter-order requirement and that the result must match an online BMI calculator.
Add a live BMI form in the explore demo with inputs for kilograms and metres.
Mention Math.pow(height, 2) as an alternative to height * height.
